extracted.intended_audience: managers, analysts, and policymakers in the Department of Defense military health services system (MTF managers, ER/CA planners, and financial/reporting staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for designing, implementing, and reporting productivity/efficiency measures and cost-accounting (UCA) for Department of Defense medical treatment facilities. Covers desirable measure properties, data requirements, peer-grouping, proposed performance indicators, and UCA reporting structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perverse or negative incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology and the measure should avoid perverse or negative incentives for the entity measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures should not encourage behavior that reduces true efficiency or quality in order to improve measured performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulative potential of input variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should avoid manipulative potential of the input variables by interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose inputs that cannot be easily manipulated by those being measured; design safeguards to reduce gaming of inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available, identifiable, representative inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should rely on inputs that are available, easy to identify and representative of the actual inputs that go into the transformation process of the entity and result in the entity's products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer data sources that are routinely collected and clearly map to the production process to reduce measurement error and workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of implementation and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should be relatively simple to implement, use, and understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex measures risk implementation failure; balance analytical rigor with operational feasibility and comprehension by stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce single-valued, understandable results
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should produce results that are single valued and understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear numeric indicators (rather than ambiguous indices) so decision makers can readily interpret performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology must be inexpensive and not labor intensive
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should incorporate a methodology that is inexpensive and not labor intensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid measures that impose high data collection or processing costs relative to their decision value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize subjectivity in inputs/process
rubrics_metrics.description: The input process should eliminate as much of the subjective as is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use objective, standardized definitions and procedures to reduce bias and improve comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reference to quality of performance in efficiency measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The efficiency measure should avoid any reference to quality of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efficiency measures should focus on resource use/output; quality should be measured separately to avoid confounding incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate costs with performance
rubrics_metrics.description: To be useful for resource planning, budgeting, and management, the measure should associate costs with performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures that link cost and performance enable meaningful resource-allocation and budgeting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer cost per beneficiary (or cost per patient episode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any measure developed probably should reflect a cost per beneficiary or cost per patient episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: commonality across service measures, less manipulable by activity measured, and avoidance of perverse incentives. Disadvantages: does not fully explain drivers of demand/cost and may omit nuanced outputs captured by cost-per-output measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with cost-per-output surrogate labels
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost per output inclusion in the measure would suffer the disadvantage of too many surrogate labels for difficult to define outputs and have few of the advantages of the cost per beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using proxies like occupied bed days or outpatient visits can be manipulated and may not represent aggregate output well unless homogeneity assumptions hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cost/percentage (ratio) relationships appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost/percentage relationship (ratio of two costs) can illustrate relationship changes over time for specific activities or functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ratios are useful to identify abnormalities but should be specifically related to what they are intended to measure; they are diagnostic rather than comprehensive performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link measurement to incentive schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency Review directives stress the need for relating measurement, evaluation, and analysis of productivity to some incentive scheme that induces efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ideal measure would itself contain an incentive for efficiency and express the value in a manner permitting observation of actual cost per unit; measures used for ER/CA should be usable in incentive designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of data and variable definitions across MTFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of MTF data and definitions of variables/characteristics is required to improve representation of productivity by proxy measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized definitions across facilities improve comparability and reduce classification and measurement errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full cost identification and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Full cost identification, full cost identification and recognition (full-costing) is necessary for accurate representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify both direct and indirect costs where practical so measures reflect true resource consumption; support comparability to civilian structures where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform isolation of non-direct patient care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of non-direct patient care cost isolation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently separate non-patient-care (nonmission) costs so direct patient care cost per unit is meaningful and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability to trace costs to actual patient groupings (DRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to trace costs to actual groupings of patients receiving services (e.g., DRGs) improves representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If costs can be attributed to clinically meaningful patient groupings, utilization and case-mix adjustments become more defensible and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-grouping (homogeneity) for comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical facilities should be grouped to bring homogeneity using variables (size by beds, number of services, types of services, teaching/residency programs, number of admissions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer grouping must be as objective and neutrally fair as possible; changes in grouping materially affect workload weighting and should be decided at the highest common-interest level (e.g., OASD(HA)). Polythetic clustering analysis is the recommended technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ratio of actual to expected output as a basic standard
rubrics_metrics.description: One basic standard selected: actual amounts of output / expected amounts of output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ratio yields 1 for expected performance, <1 for inefficiency, and >1 for above-expected efficiency; allows comparisons over time and across similar facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cost per expected facility utilization metric
rubrics_metrics.description: A modified model: actual period costs / expected facility utilization — produces an average cost per expected beneficiary utilization meaningful to decision makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates costs to expected utilization across facilities (e.g., compare direct patient care costs to expected facility utilization for two clinics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include four core data elements in proposed performance indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure incorporates four elements: (1) facility total adjusted costs, (2) beneficiary groupings for demographic representation, (3) incidence rates of expected utilization, and (4) an adjustment factor for intensity of services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements permit adjustment for population mix, utilization incidence, and service intensity to make cost per expected beneficiary comparable across facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize unit prices and avoid uncontrollable cost elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Total cost data element should be obtained from internal sources; to reduce variance, each unit price can be standardized for the period (e.g., standardize labor by averaged billet cost, energy by price per kilowatt hour). The measure should avoid inclusion of cost elements not controllable and not direct patient care for local health care delivery cost centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization reduces variance and improves comparability; exclude costs outside local control to prevent misleading accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical cost element categories for proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of complexity, actual cost elements might be represented, in proxy, by the following cost elements: labor, material, equipment, energy, and overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standardized categories when detailed case-level costing is infeasible; document proxy assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary grouping criteria and common categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Group beneficiaries by attributes common to populations (income, age, sex) and use standard beneficiary classes: (1) active duty personnel, (2) active duty dependents, (3) retired personnel, (4) retired dependents, (5) survivors of active duty and retired sponsors. Subdivide by enlisted/officer and rank; use age bands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homogeneous grouping based on attributes reduces heterogeneity; use DOD sources such as DEERS for demographic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include incidence-rate adjustment factor for intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: The incidence rate adjustment factor reflects the intensity of resource allocation necessary for a given incidence rate of a specified event. Adjustment factors can be adapted from reference sources (California Relative Value Studies) or developed locally at the peer-grouping/regional level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute incidence as number of events during period / population at risk; typically expressed per 1,000. Use incidence to adjust expected utilization by event class (e.g., inpatient dispositions, outpatient visits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider DRGs for utilization representation
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the thesis, the use of DRGs appears most promising as a representation of utilization in a performance measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DRGs provide clinically meaningful grouping of cases that support case-mix adjustment and tracing of costs to patient groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCA purpose: consistent principles and performance accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: The UCA's purpose: 'provide consistent principles, standards, policies, definitions, and requirements for expense and performance accounting and reporting by DOD fixed military medical facilities' and support measurement of productivity, development of performance and cost standards, and informational tools to focus attention on inefficiency and poor management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCA is the standardization vehicle to enable intra-/inter-service and civilian comparisons and to support management decision-making and strategic planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCA objectives (six targeted uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UCA was targeted toward six objectives: (1) commonality of definition for workload, work centers, and respective cost accounts, (2) a broader, more specific database for use in management reports, (3) a way to apply performance measurement for internal/external comparisons, (4) a means of efficiency and cost measurement, (5) process of overhead and ancillary service expense allocation procedures, and (6) provide information for productivity measurement and resource allocation efficiency evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design UCA data collection and coding to fulfill these objectives and to be complementary to military accounting systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCA step-down accounting and code hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: As a cost accounting system, the UCA steps-down overall cost assignments into final, commonly defined, operating expense accounts via a hierarchy of functional categories, summary accounts, subaccounts, and optional fourth-level local codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use UCA codes consistently (A-F functional categories) and apply stepdown methodology to allocate intermediate account costs to final accounts; use 'X' pool accounts, temporary '4' codes and 'Z'/'Y' coding per guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define output measures by UCA functional category
rubrics_metrics.description: Each functional category has cost and workload collection to produce some cost per unit of workload: inpatient (cost per occupied bed day), ambulatory care (visits), dental (weighted procedures), ancillary (prescriptions, hours of service), support services (square footage or pro rata), pooled accounts not measured by unit cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate output metric per functional category; recognize intermediary accounts are allocated rather than given their own efficiency metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCA reporting: Computation Summary and Detailed Unit Cost Report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Computation Summary provides functional account and categorical summaries (direct/ancillary/support/pool costs) and the Detailed Unit Cost Report details total expenses, output measures, and a cost per unit of output for local management analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these reports to examine deviant unit costs, trace false deviations to stepdown or data entry errors, and support intra-/inter-facility comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize UCA limitations (not full cost accounting or activity management system)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UCA is not an expense and workload collection system in the full cost-accounting sense; many UCA accounts do not correspond to specific organizational units and the system lacks some characteristics of full cost accounting and activity-based management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must understand limitations: UCA collects expenses (not all features of cost accounting), shared services may not be controllable by consuming services, and cost objectives may not directly support activity-level management needs.
